digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI workflows and gate scripts
propositions: The pre-gate-guard shell pattern '[[ -f <path> ]] || { echo "change predates the gate" ; exit 0 ; }' appears 24 times across six workflow files and action.yml, with recent copies drifting (anxious-resistant-urson missing a guard, sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly adding one late).

The guard cannot be moved into a shared repo file because such a file is absent on exactly the pre-gate trees the guard serves, causing a composite action or helper to either incorrectly skip existing scripts or fail on missing local uses.
Two scripts (check_readme_quickstart.py, probe_rebar.py) are guarded in gerrit-verify.yaml but not guarded identically in test.yml, reproducing the pattern of bug anxious-resistant-urson.

A parity test must assert that every gate step in the six files either carries an -f guard with the canonical message or bears a mandatory-reason # predates-gate-ok: marker, and that every guarded step body exits 0 with that message when run in an empty directory.

The four gates (plan-review close, plan-review claim, completion close, code-review dispatch) already share uniform ref resolution through gate_source.resolve_gate_handle and three share a single gate_enabled function; code_review_enabled must retain its divergent broad-except/silent-false behavior.

No new guards are added and no existing guards removed in this story, because adding a guard changes which gates run on old bases and is its own reviewable change; genuine guard gaps are instead filed and linked as discovered_from rather than fixed here.
